title: Read all result pages
summary: A Query response can be only one page of data.
introduction: A Query response can be only one page of data. Your task: Find the continuation key after querying a multi-item partition.
learningObjectives: Find the continuation key after querying a multi-item partition.
Explain the example for read all result pages

blocks.text: A Query response can be only one page of data. LastEvaluatedKey tells the caller where to continue.

Use DynamoDB Local and the AWS CLI or SDK in a separate practice project. Point every command at http://localhost:8000. Low-level JSON examples show request bodies; provide them to the matching CLI command or SDK method.
Read the code step by step

items: `KeyConditionExpression` uses the table or index keys to select a partition and, optionally, a sort-key range.
`ConditionExpression` checks the current item as part of the write, so a failed condition prevents the change.
`ExpressionAttributeNames` maps placeholders such as #reader to actual field names in the request expression.

blocks.text: With several sample items, the response may include LastEvaluatedKey. Pass it as ExclusiveStartKey in the next request.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Limit is not a promise that you have read the whole partition. Continue until no LastEvaluatedKey remains.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Find the continuation key after querying a multi-item partition.
